content: The throttle position sensor reports throttle plate angle to the ECM. A failing TPS causes incorrect fuel delivery, hesitation, and poor idle. Inspect sensor voltage sweep from closed to open throttle for smooth transition.

The accelerator pedal position sensor reports driver throttle demand to the ECM. A failing APP sensor causes hesitation, incorrect throttle response, or limp mode. Inspect sensor voltage sweep and correlate with throttle body position.

The intake air temperature sensor reports ambient air temperature to the ECM. The ECM uses this to adjust fuel delivery. A failing IAT sensor causes incorrect fuel mixture, rough idle, and hesitation. Inspect sensor resistance vs temperature.

The engine coolant temperature sensor reports engine temperature to the ECM. The ECM uses this for fuel enrichment, idle control, and transmission shift points. A failing ECT sensor causes poor cold-start, incorrect fuel mixture, and overheating warnings. Inspect sensor resistance vs temperature.

The crankshaft position sensor provides engine speed and piston position to the ECM. The ECM uses this for fuel injection timing and ignition control. A failing CKP sensor causes no-start, stalling, and misfire codes. Inspect sensor resistance and air gap.

The camshaft position sensor provides camshaft position to the ECM. The ECM uses this for sequential fuel injection and variable valve timing control. A failing CMP sensor causes rough running, no-start, and poor timing control. Inspect sensor resistance and reluctor ring.

The knock sensor detects engine detonation and signals the ECM to retard ignition timing. A failing knock sensor causes pinging, reduced power, and potential engine damage under load. Inspect sensor resistance and torque specification.
